shared_elements: figures rendered in flat profile silhouette against a plain ground
quadruped animal seen from the side
a horizontal band of repeated small marks (rows of strokes / zigzag register)
isolated motifs distributed over an unframed natural stone surface
justification: Both surfaces carry small profile figures and at least one circular disc set against bare stone with a horizontal band of repeating marks, which is the most specific correspondence, but the resemblance stops at that generic level. A is painted red-brown silhouette work scattered irregularly across a sloping rock face, while B is low relief carved in registers on an upright rectangular pillar, so the manner of execution and the compositional logic are fundamentally unlike.
